source.title: On the Limitations of Fractal Dimension as a Measure of Generalization
source.authors: Charlie B. Tan; Inés García-Redondo; Qi-Quan Wang; M. Bronstein; Anthea Monod

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests persistent-homology dimensions as generalization-gap measures and reports failures, confounding, and settings where their relationship is absent or conditional.
record.gate_note: The study measures correlations and conditional dependence between PH dimensions and accuracy/loss gaps. It also reports training accuracy as a convergence criterion; that is setup, not a separate result row. The double-descent test-accuracy pattern is not itself a generalization-gap measure and is not extracted as a row.
record.test_reason: Section 6 reports test accuracy across CNN widths on CIFAR-100, including improvement after the double-descent critical region, bearing on V2 in a new setting. The PH-dimension experiments do not test V7: trajectory fractal dimension is a different measure from magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: PH dimensions are not universally reliable correlates of generalization gaps; hyperparameters can confound associations, and adversarial initialization and width variation reveal failures. These findings concern PH dimensions, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: Follows Dupuis et al. (2023): SGD to convergence, then samples 5000 additional iterations and estimates Euclidean and loss-based 0-PH dimensions. Adds partial-correlation, conditional-independence, adversarial-initialization, and width-variation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and batch size influence observed correlations; initialization and width variation alter or break the relationship. The paper reports no explicit regularization, constant learning rates, vanilla SGD, and no batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: PH dimensions have positive aggregate gap correlations in most grid experiments, but AlexNet's loss-based correlation is negative; conditioning reveals hyperparameter dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization-trajectory PH dimensions sometimes correlate with generalization gaps, with associations sensitive to architecture and hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial initialization produces misleading PH-dimension rankings for CNN CIFAR-10 and FCN-5 MNIST, while AlexNet rankings have the expected direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PH dimensions do not reliably rank generalization gaps across initialization schemes.

fits_no_version.finding: Neither PH dimension tracks the generalization gap across CNN widths, although Euclidean PH dimension exhibits a double-descent pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory PH dimension can track width-dependent test-accuracy structure without tracking the training-test gap.

record.problems: The study uses a limited range of learning rates and batch sizes; CIFAR-10 grid experiments use one seed; double-descent experiments use three seeds and omit batch normalization and learning-rate decay; PH computation is costly; width-specific numerical correlations are not tabulated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No required result rows omitted. The double-descent pattern in test accuracy and Euclidean PH dimension is not extracted as a row because V7 concerns tracking the training-test gap, and the text says neither PH dimension correlates with that gap in this setting.

untested.parts: The paired natural-label and random-label held-out performance comparison; random-label interpolation is used to construct an initialization.
The original one-hidden-layer setting, training to convergence at every width, and a numerical identification of the zero-training-error threshold are not established here.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance; grid runs instead train to convergence.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
All parts: magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness is not measured, nor compared with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal followed by retraining.

missing.what: Add the qualitative width-versus-test-accuracy result relevant to V2, including improvement after the double-descent critical region. Exact accuracies and interpolation widths cannot be recovered from the supplied figure caption and prose.

record.verdict_notes: The record's exclusion of double-descent test accuracy overlooks V2, so that explicitly declared omission still needs correction. The supplied text supports a qualitative widening result, but does not establish convergence or exact interpolation thresholds for the width sweep. Conditional-independence non-rejection does not prove independence or establish causality.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization and chance test accuracy on random labels.
Widening beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
The specific magnitude-aware sharpness measure and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100 standard CNN, widening beyond the double-descent critical region; vanilla SGD, constant learning rate 0.01, batch size 128, 250,000-iteration cap, three seeds.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 6 and Figure 4 rather than an extracted row: the authors report classical double descent in test accuracy, including recovery with further widening. This supports the post-critical widening trend qualitatively.
relationships.display_finding: The reported recovery in test accuracy beyond the critical width region remains unverified.
